A Bullion Trading Tradition
धनतेरस
Dhanteras — The Most Auspicious Day to Buy Gold & Silver
Once a year, on Dhanteras, families bring home a small piece of gold or silver to welcome Lakshmi. For many in the US it is a once-a-year ritual — so the questions are the same every time. Here is a plain-English guide to the day, the metal, and what to buy.
Educational only — festival dates and muhurat vary by panchang; confirm your local timings.
धनतेरस
श्री
DHANTERAS
Once a year, on
Dhanteras
, millions of families bring home a small piece of gold or silver. It is the first of Diwali’s five days and, by long tradition, the single most auspicious day to buy precious metal — a way to welcome
Lakshmi
, the goddess of wealth, into the home for the year ahead. The word itself says it:
dhan
(wealth) +
teras
(the thirteenth lunar day).
For many families in the US this is a once-a-year ritual, and the questions are the same every time — gold or silver? a coin or a bar? how much? This is a plain-English guide to the day, the metal, and what to buy.
The day
Nov 6
Dhanteras 2026 — day one of the five-day Diwali festival
Bought in a day
20–35t
of gold across India — its single busiest gold-buying day
What matters
The act
tradition values the buying itself — even a 1-gram token
Why gold and silver on Dhanteras
The custom traces to the
Samudra Manthan
, the churning of the cosmic ocean. From it rose
Dhanvantari
, physician of the gods and father of Ayurveda, carrying the pot of
amrita
(the nectar of immortality) — and from the same ocean arose Lakshmi herself, holding a pot of gold, together with
Kuber
, treasurer of the gods. Dhanteras is Dhanvantari’s appearance day, which is why the day ties wealth to health, and why bringing new metal home is believed to invite Lakshmi and “multiply” prosperity.
A second, beloved legend explains the lamps: a young prince fated to die of snakebite was saved when his bride heaped gold and silver at the doorway and kept lamps blazing all night — Yama, arriving as a serpent, was dazzled by the glitter and spared him. Families still light 13
diyas
, the first placed outside facing south as a
Yama Deepam
for protection.
On Diwali night proper, Lakshmi is worshipped not alone but with
Ganesha
, remover of obstacles and lord of wisdom — so that wealth arrives with the good sense to keep it. Silver carries its own meaning as the metal of
Chandra
, the Moon: purity, coolness, and calm.
Thirteen diyas are lit on Dhanteras — the first, the Yama Deepam, is placed outside facing south for protection.
Reason
What it means
Invites Lakshmi
Bringing new gold or silver home welcomes the goddess of wealth and is believed to multiply prosperity.
Honors the Manthan deities
Lakshmi, Kuber, and Dhanvantari all rose from the churned ocean — metal honors abundance and health together.
The King Hima legend
Gold and silver at the door once dazzled Yama and saved a life, tying metal to protection as well as wealth.
Silver is the Moon
Silver is Chandra’s metal — purity, calm, cooling energy — favored for puja vessels and gifting.
A real store of value
A small coin or bar is liquid, easily kept, and a steadying asset when markets are uncertain.
The threads that make precious metal the gift of the day.
The five days of Diwali
Dhanteras opens a five-day festival, each day with its own meaning. In 2026 they fall Friday, November 6 through Tuesday, November 10.

What to buy — and how much
The signature Dhanteras purchase is a small
silver Lakshmi-Ganesh coin
— Lakshmi for wealth, Ganesh to clear the way — kept in the home shrine and worshipped at Lakshmi Puja. Gold is bought too, and increasingly as coins and small bars rather than jewelry, for their higher purity, lower premium, and easy resale.
It’s the act, not the amount.
Dhanteras tradition holds that the auspiciousness lies in
acquiring
metal, not in how much you spend. Historically even the poorest households buy something small — a single gram of silver, a steel vessel, even coriander seeds — to welcome Lakshmi. Buy within your means; a token counts as much as an heirloom.

24-karat purity, low premium, global liquidity, clean resale — a store of value that still carries the auspicious theme.

Why families now choose coins and bars
Gold’s price has climbed steeply over the past decade. As it hit records, Indian buyers shifted hard toward small 1–50 gram coins and bars — higher purity, no jewelry “making charges,” and cleaner buyback. On Dhanteras 2025 the shift was dramatic: silver coins and bars actually
out-sold
gold, with silver’s sales value more than doubling.

Relatives may talk in

The auspicious time to buy
Many families buy during the day’s
shubh muhurat
— an auspicious window, often around the evening
Pradosh Kaal
when Lakshmi and Kuber are worshipped — though the whole of Dhanteras is considered favorable. Times shift by city and by the
panchang
used, so confirm your local timing. If you’re shipping within the US, the practical advice is simple:
order early
so your piece is in hand for the puja.

Common Questions
Questions families ask us
What should I buy on Dhanteras if I only want one thing?
The traditional choice is a small silver Lakshmi-Ganesh coin — Lakshmi for wealth, Ganesh to remove obstacles — kept in the home shrine and worshipped at Lakshmi Puja. A 1-gram gold bar or a 1 oz silver Diwali bar are equally auspicious “token” options.
Does it matter how much I spend?
No. Tradition holds that the auspiciousness is in the act of acquiring metal, not the amount. Even the poorest households historically buy something small — a gram of silver, a steel vessel, even coriander seeds — to welcome Lakshmi. Buy within your means.
Should I buy 24K or 22K?
For a Dhanteras purchase meant as a store of value or gift, 24K (.999/.9999) coins and bars are usually best: higher purity, lower premiums, universal recognition, and easier resale. 22K (916) is the jewelry standard — more durable to wear, but harder to price and resell as bullion.
Why are the PAMP “Diwali Lakshmi” bars a good fit?
PAMP Suisse mints them specifically for the festival: .9999 gold (or .999 silver) struck with Lakshmi and rangoli artwork, sealed in a colorized assay card with a unique serial number. They combine investment-grade purity with a giftable, festival-appropriate presentation, in 5-gram and 1-ounce sizes.
My family talks about “tola” and “sovereign” — what are those in US terms?
They are weights, not purities. One tola = 11.6638 grams, one sovereign (pavan) = 8 grams, and one troy ounce (how US dealers sell) = 31.1035 grams. A “sovereign” can be 22K or 24K depending on the item.
What is a muhurat — do I have to buy at an exact time?
A muhurat is an auspicious time window on Dhanteras, often around the evening Pradosh Kaal when Lakshmi and Kuber are worshipped. Many families buy during it, but the whole day is considered favorable — so if you’re shipping within the US, order early enough to have the piece in hand for the puja. Confirm your local timing with a panchang.
Coins, bars, or jewelry — what are buyers choosing now?
The trend, sharpened by record prices, is strongly toward coins and small bars (1–50 grams) over jewelry, for higher purity, no making charges, and cleaner resale. On Dhanteras 2025, silver coins and bars even out-sold gold, with silver’s sales value more than doubling.
How do I know a coin or bar is genuine if it has no BIS hallmark?
BIS hallmarking with its HUID code is India’s system. Reputable international mints instead ship each piece in a sealed, serialized assay card (for example PAMP’s CertiPAMP) stating the fineness. Buying from an established dealer with the original assay packaging is the equivalent assurance for a US buyer.
Preparing for Dhanteras 2026?
Dhanteras falls on Friday, November 6. Order early so your Lakshmi bar or coin is in hand for the puja — we ship nationwide, and can help you choose the right size and metal for your family’s custom.
